scenes.text: What if you ate only instant noodles for thirty days? Breakfast, lunch and dinner, just noodles. Sounds like a dream for many people, right? But what would really happen to your body, your energy and your health? Let us find out, based on what nutrition experts say. This is for learning, not medical advice.

First, why do we love noodles? They are cheap, quick, tasty and ready in just two minutes. A hot bowl on a rainy day, or a late night while studying, feels like comfort. Nothing wrong with enjoying them sometimes. The question is what happens when it is the only food.

So what is inside a pack? Mostly refined flour, oil, salt and a tasty masala. The noodles are usually fried or air dried, so they cook fast. A pack gives you energy from carbohydrates and fat, but very little protein, fibre, vitamins or minerals.

In the first few days, you may feel happy. Your tummy is full, your tongue is happy, and you have energy from the carbohydrates. Many people say the first days are the best. But your body is only getting a small part of what it needs.

The biggest problem is salt. Many packs have a large part of the daily limit of salt in just one serving. The World Health Organization suggests less than five grams of salt a day for adults. If you eat three packs a day, you can cross this limit easily.

Too much salt makes your body hold extra water, and this raises blood pressure. Over many weeks, high blood pressure puts stress on your heart and your blood vessels. You may also notice puffy fingers or a swollen face.

The next thing missing is fibre. Fibre comes from vegetables, fruits, dals and whole grains. Without it, you can feel constipated and bloated, and the good bacteria in your gut do not get their food. Noodles are made mostly from refined flour, so they give very little.

Protein is also low. Your muscles, skin and hair need protein every day. After a few weeks with too little, you may feel weak and tired, you may lose muscle, and your hair may become dull and fall more. Wounds also heal slowly.

Now vitamins and minerals. With no fruits, vegetables or milk, you may miss vitamin C, vitamin A, calcium, iron and others. Over time, this can cause a weak immune system, bleeding gums, tiredness and pale skin. Some noodle brands add a few vitamins, but it is not enough.

By the second week, many people get bored of the taste. You may feel tired, sleepy after eating, and hungry again soon. This is because refined flour is digested quickly. You feel full for a short time, and then you want more.

Refined flour can raise your blood sugar fast, and then it falls fast. That is why you may feel energy ups and downs. For people with diabetes or at risk, this is more worrying, and they should talk to their doctor.
Your stomach may also complain. Spicy, salty and oily food again and again can cause acidity, burning and gas. Some people also feel nausea. Eating only one food gives your gut no variety.
Food also affects mood and focus. When your body lacks nutrients and your sugar level keeps jumping, you can feel low, cranky and unable to concentrate. Studying or working becomes harder.

By week four, the signs add up. You may feel constantly tired, with weak muscles, dry skin, hair fall and a weak defence against infections. A doctor might also find high blood pressure. Your body would clearly be asking for real food.

Studies suggest that people who eat instant noodles very often tend to have a poorer diet and a higher risk of heart and metabolic problems. But scientists also remind us that this does not prove noodles alone are the cause. The overall diet matters most.

Now some myths. One, noodles are made of plastic. Wrong, this is a rumour. Two, noodles stay in your stomach for days. Also wrong. Your body digests them in the normal way. Three, noodles are poison. No, they are fine in small amounts, but they are not a full meal.

If you love noodles, you can make them better. Add lots of vegetables, an egg or some paneer for protein, and use only half the masala. Drain some of the water to reduce salt. Eat them once in a while, and not every day.
If you have been eating mostly one kind of food and feel weak, dizzy or very tired, please talk to a doctor or a dietitian. Do not start a strict diet on your own. Every body is different.

So the lesson is simple. A food is not good or bad by itself. The problem is eating only one thing. Enjoy your noodles, but keep colour on your plate with vegetables, dal, fruits and protein. Variety is the secret.

So that was what would happen if you ate only instant noodles for thirty days. If you liked this video, please like and subscribe to Professor Alienstein for more what-if science. Which food should I test next? Tell me in the comments!
